rationale: Round 1 ran at the 7.02 ns floor with 0.4 ns margins and cut T_eff to 6.33/6.34. Both runs are feasible: 0 hold buffers, 0 slew/cap pins (bar 309), DRC clears, wirelength ~9% over the estimate. The worst path (ss 100C max-RC) touches a port, but reg-to-reg trails it by only 0.03-0.05 ns. Both runs match despite different util/density/slew, so repair at the floor target with max margins looks binding. Keep those pins, cap213, post-GRT timing repair and timing-driven placement. The remaining lever is intrinsic logic delay: the only AREA 3 runs without ABC sizing/buffering had the fastest reg-to-reg (6.14/6.22 vs 6.29-6.44 ns). Test SYNTH_SIZING=false while the optimizer keeps ABC buffering, which may protect port paths.
